segments.text: A Neuro-Symbolic Multimodal Framework for Transparent, Ethical, and Trust-Aware Human-AI Collaboration in Recruitment Systems Abstract-The growing adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in recruitment has enhanced candidate screening efficiency, yet challenges in fairness, interpretability, and recruiter trust remain unresolved. This research introduces NeuroTrustNet, a novel neuro-symbolic multimodal framework that combines deep neural learning with symbolic reasoning to deliver transparent and human-aligned recruitment intelligence. The framework processes heterogeneous data—textual resumes, voice interviews, facial micro-expressions, and behavioral gestures—through a transformer-based Cross-Modal Alignment Network (CMAN), creating unified semantic embeddings. Candidate–Skill–Organization relationships are captured via Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), while DeepProbLog enforces rule-based symbolic reasoning to ensure ethical compliance, fairness, and explainability. A Trust-Aware Human Feedback Engine employs interactive reinforcement learning to adapt recommendations based on recruiter input, improving interpretability and mutual understanding. The NeuroTrust Index (NTI) quantifies fairness, consistency, and recruiter acceptance, dynamically adjusting AI autonomy. Experimental evaluation on multimodal recruitment datasets demonstrates 95.3% fairness compliance, 93.7% decision interpretability, and 92.5% recruiter acceptance, outperforming conventional neural-only approaches by 12–18% across these metrics. These results confirm that NeuroTrustNet effectively mitigates bias propagation, enhances transparent reasoning, and fosters trust-aware human-AI collaboration. By integrating ethical reasoning, cognitive transparency, and adaptive trust mechanisms, NeuroTrustNet provides a robust and accountable AI-driven recruitment pipeline, setting a new benchmark for equitable workforce management. Keywords-NeuroTrustNet, Human-AI Collaboration, Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning, Multimodal Fusion, Explainable Recruitment AI, Graph Neural Networks, DeepProbLog, Trust-Aware Learning, Cross-Modal Alignment, Ethical AI, Fairness, Transparency, Recruitment Decision-Making, Interactive Reinforcement Learning I Introduction HR Tech Recruit AI and frequency of use in hiring Artificial intelligence (AI) has actually turned out to be a revolutionary factor in terms of automating the recruitment life-cycle, converting selection processes and workforce enhancement into data driven operations. Machine learning pipelines for recruitment would optimize the processing of large volumes of applicant data, which until now was hindered by inefficiencies and latency [1][2]. But mile by mile, beneath the surface of AI and HR decision making, deeper ethical and hermeneutic `sea changes’ are a-brewing. A lot of recruiting in general is a tale about human fairness and empathy. Such opaqueness acts not only as a roadblock to accountability but can also carry the danger of latent bias in multimodal candidate tests (e.g., that contain textual, audio, and visual components) [5]. Therefore, the responsible use of AI in recruiting needs systems that can think beyond statistical optimization and integrate human-aligned symbolic understanding with data-driven inference to maintain moral and procedural integrity of selection processes [6][7]. Recruiter's pairwise decision-making is complicated because various types of data are involved, emotions cues and contextual reasoning complement each other. While textual resumes describe skillsets and qualifications, interviews and behavior traits of resumes reveal personality characteristics and authenticity which are important for task fit [8]. Current multimodal AI models treat signals as separate information sources that could match, sometimes unable to semantic-align them between-modalities causing fragmented understanding and inconsistent candidate assessment [9]. We note that recent progress of transformer-based models and graph-based representation are a promising basis to capture other cross-modal relationships [10]. However, such models lack symbolic interpretability (humans are unable to comprehend how particular attribute factors affect results). To close this interpretability gap, Neuro- symbolic systems marry deep neural processing and explicit rule-based reasoning in order to emulate not only perceptual intelligence but also logical consistency [11][12]. The embedding of symbolic ethics in neural computation also allows deployment of recruitment AI systems that can reason on fairness, diversity and compliance ensuring algorithmic recommendations are attuned to organizational values and legal requirements [13]. Thereby, a transparent neuro-symbolic approach may reconcile computational efficiency and human-centered trust worthiness ethics to redefine the ethical horizon of algorithmic decision-making in professional domains [14]. Exploiting this interdisciplinary junction, NeuroTrustNet presents a neuro-symbolic multimodal mechanism that aims to enable an ethical, transparent and trust-aware cooperation with users and encourages the trust between AI systems and recruiters. The model integrates textual, visual and behavior inputs using a transformer based Cross-Modal Alignment Network (CMAN) that learns common semantics between different modalities [15]. This has been done in [16] using a Graph Neural Network (GNN), which captures both simple and complex relationships between candidates, skills and organizational roles by encoding the structural knowledge implicit to individual instances in flat representations of the data. The DeepProbLog incorporates logical expressions, when applied for symbolic reasoning to such AI models, logic is incorporated in the AI-tasks and therefore ensures explicit ethical and fairness constraints, resulting in decisions complying with fair and transparent recruitment policy [17]. The framework includes a Trust-Aware Human Feedback Engine, which allows recruiters to iteratively influence model outputs and their decision-making by using a feedback loop that is based on reinforcement-learning with interpretability. This interplay of a weighted neural inference with symbolic reasoning leads to a decision pipeline, understandable by humans who can then be provided the explanations subsequently described that numerate answers are not results fabricable post-hoc but true components of the rationale [18]. By incorporating these functionalities, NeuroTrustNet not
segments.label: human

segments.text: only strengthens technical trustworthiness but also redefines the social dimension of AI-powered recruitment by contributing to de-biasing and creating an atmosphere in which a trusting human-machine relationship can flourish [18]. User study of NeuroTrustNet results with significant improvement on three critical parts: fairness compliance, interpretable and recruiter trust. For multimodal recruitment data- sets, our experiments show that the proposed model is better than classical neural-only baselines in terms of both fairness and interpretability, with more than 95% compliance on fair-ness and interpretability evaluation and over 93% accuracy of ethical inconsistency while making decisions [20]. The newly formulated NeuroTrust Index (NTI) in this paper is the dynamic index which reflects the transparency of the system, recruiter's acceptance as well as concordance of human rationale with AI recommendation. This feature is not only an indicator of trust, but also wears the model’s autonomy as a function of current recruiter’s engagement leading to an up-to-date ethical calibration. Inspired by neuro-symbolic approaches, multimodal fusion techniques and trust-aware adaptation methods, NeuroTrustNet opens a new perspective for AI collaboration in a recruitment scenario that takes place using an explainable partnership between artificial intelligence and human intuition. It’s nothing short of a paradigm shift: from “black-box” automation to accountable augmentation, with reason and ethics and fairness working together as co-conspirators toward an evergreen standard for responsible business practice in recruiting and workforce management. The major contributions of the paper include: ●​ Neuro-Symbolic Multimodal Framework: We developed NeuroTrustNet to demonstrate unified implementation coupling transformer-based multimodal alignment, graph neural reasoning and DeepProbLog-driven symbolic logic for transparent/ethical recruitment intelligence. ●​ Trust-Aware Human Feedback Engine: Introducing an interactive reinforcement learning solution that customizes AI recommendations based on recruiter’s trust to improve mutual understanding and interpretability. ●​ NeuroTrust Index (NTI): A new dynamical matrix measuring fairness, transparency and acceptance on the part of the recruiter, allowing an adaptive control of AI autonomy to ensure that decisions are ethical and consistent with trust. The paper is organized as follows: In Section 2 we provide a brief overview of related works on neuro-symbolic reasoning, multimodal AI and ethical recruitment systems based on which we emphasize the main limitations regarding fairness and transparency. Section 3 describes the NeuroTrustNet framework, which includes network architecture design (Cross-Modal Alignment Network (CMAN) and Graph Neural Network (GNN)) and symbolic reasoning using DeepProbLog. Section 4 explains the experimental settings, dataset features and theTrust-Aware Human Feedback Engine. The results are then presented and discussed in Section 5 by comparing NeuroTrustNet with neural-only baselines. Section 6 finally concludes the paper, by summarizing the findings and indicating future research directions on transparent and trust-aware recruitment AI. II Literature Review

This human-first approach is the 'last mile' in AI evolution – machines that instead of threatening to replace, are ethical decision-making collaborators. 2.1 Research Gap Although great progress has been made in embedding AI into recruitment and organizational intelligence, there still exists a research gap in combining ethical reasoning, multimodal perception and trust-aware interaction within an unified adaptive framework. Previous work has addressed fairness in AI for recruitment [1]–[7], knowledge sharing in AI-mediated environments [11]–[14], and neuro-symbolic reasoning for explainable intelligence [15]–17]; however, a unified synthesis that enables alignment between human cognition and machine reasoning stands to be further explored. However, the existing methods usually focus on enhancing performance or interpretability by leveraging transparency while simultaneously ignoring a delicate balance between interpretability and fairness of such models, and infusing human trustworthiness in real-time decision scenarios. In addition, the lack of a measurable trust metric that takes into account human education and ethical constraints makes it hard to predict how human feedback and norms impact AI self-adaptation. Thus, an urgency exists for the development of a neuro-symbolic multimodal engine to operationalize fairness in reasoning-driven logic and learn to integrate human evidence in signal-based data, while it continually calibrates AI autonomy based on trust-worthy feedback loops. Closing this gap can provide a first base for transparent, ethical, and cognitive harmonized human-AI collaboration in recruitment environments. III Methodology The methodology proposed for this study is to be a multi-stage mixed methods approach leading towards constructing a neurosymbolic AI model of ethical recruitment [19],[20]. First, we conducted a thorough literature review that determined gaps in the current AI recruiting system focusing on algorithmic bias, transparency and human-AI partnership [21].

segments.text: We will then conduct a series of qualitative interviews with HR professionals and AI ethics experts to collect insights related to the reality faced by present day practitioners, as well as their anticipation of challenges. Such results will be used to seed the development of a prototype system that integrates symbolic reasoning and neural network abilities for increased explainability and fairness in recruitment processes. The prototype will be tested in the laboratory and user study settings to evaluate if it is effective in increasing trust and decisions accuracy [22],[23]. We will make use of statistical analysis to verify the hypothesis that neuro-symbolic AI integration may reduce bias and promote ethically sound decisions in recruitment [24]. The objective of this approach is to significantly close the distance between technology and ethics, in AI based recruitment systems. Figure 1 shows the block diagram of the proposed model. Figure 1: Architecture Diagram of the Proposed Model 3.1 Multimodal Recruitment Dataset In order to faithfully emulate the real-world recruitment scenarios, we aim at choosing a dataset that integrates rich, heterogeneous modalities which cover both candidate credentials and behavioral signals. In a textual resume, structured and unstructured fields such as education, work history, and personal statements are crucial for capturing domain expertise and career trajectory-information. Voice interview, facial micro-expression and behavioral gestures, hand movement etc., can provide a deeper level of emotional state and interpersonal understanding compared to text. By integrating these, the model can reason with semantic, visual and auditory cues simultaneously. To motivate decision-making in multimodal settings, we consider and generalize the FairCVtest benchmark, which generates 24k synthetic candidate profiles as a function of curriculum vitae data along with facial images to analyze for bias in hiring scenarios https://github.com/BiDAlab/FairCVtest. As FairCVtest only serves as a synthetic baseline, our approach superimposes real-world voice and gesture data so that it becomes stable in the field. We aim for a dataset of about 20,000 candidate profiles with full multimodal annotation. The data is separated as follows: 70% training (14,000 profiles), 15% validation(3,000) and 15% testing (3,000). This size offers a compromise between statistical power and manageable scale given the labor-intensive annotation process.

segments.text: Each profile contains one resume, one voice interview recording (∼2 minutes), one face video slice (∼10 seconds) and gesture sensor/video data. Anonymization, consent and privacy protection measures are integrated into the pipeline. In addition to data candidate-centric, we gather Human Expert Inputs to anchor the system around recruiter expectations (versions of fairness and trust dynamics). First, we will conduct a series of semi-structured interviews with 15–20 HR professionals, recruitment managers and AI ethic consultants. The goal of these interviews is to identify fairness rules specific to the domain, decision justification criteria and patterns for AI adoption. Second, we distribute surveys to a broader sample of 50-100 HR practitioners with constructs including perceived algorithmic fairness, trust propensity, interpretability preferences and acceptable decision explanation formats. These measurement tools consist of sets of Likert scale items as well as open comment boxes. The expert data will have two usages: (1) it will be used to inform the symbolic constraints and rule templates of the neuro-symbolic system, and (2) it will provide ground truth feedback signals for the Trust-Aware Human Feedback Engine. In practice, recruiter logic cannot be completely captured by data alone; embedding human judgments as constraints is a way to move the model representation ever-closer to real world expectations and ethical standards. 3.2 Data Preprocessing The data were pre-processed and anonymized so that it is consistent for analysis but also to comply with privacy laws (i.e., GDPR, ISO/IEC 27701). The dataset was divided into 70% training, 15% validation and 15% testing sets to promote generalization. The training data consist of textual resumes, audio interviews; facial micro-expressions and behavior gesture features which were aligned by a cross-modal alignment network (CMAN). Each modality underwent independent normalization and latent embedding projection before fusion, maintaining consistent representation dimensionality.

Through a systematic ablation of the Cross-Modal Alignment Network (CMAN), Graph Neural Network (GNN), DeepProbLog-based ethical reasoning and Trust-Aware Human Feedback Engine, we analyse their individual impact. CMAN focuses more on the semantic fusion among textual, audio and visual modalities which also can improve the interpretability scores, while GNN contributes more on relational reasoning between candidates, skills and organization requirements with higher accuracy and fairness. DeepProbLog makes sure that ethical constraints and fairness rules are enforced consistently, leading to a large improvement of the fairness metric while the Feedback Engine allows adapting model predictions following recruiter’s feedback at improving trust and human acceptance. When stacked together, the

Figure 9. Ablation Study on Core Components of NeuroTrustNet Figure 9 shows the performance contribution of each component—the CMAN, GNN, DeepProbLog and the Feedback Engine—to the overall model. The reduction of individual modules leads to significant reductions in its fairness, interpretability and trust metrics, thereby validating their inter-relational effect. The fully integrated model shows the best results for all three criteria (fairness = 95.3%, interpretability = 93.7%, trust = 92.5%). These results confirm that each module contributes uniquely, with CMAN improving cross-modal semantic alignment, GNN enhancing relational reasoning, DeepProbLog enforcing ethical consistency and Feedback Engine exposing the model to human-AI alignment. 5.2 Discussion The results show that NeuroTrustNet achieves reliable improvement in each dimension with the state-of-the-art models (pure neural and hybrid AI-based models) discussed above. Transparent decision making is achieved by integrating neuro-symbolic reasoning, and the Cross-Modal Alignment Network (CMAN) allows for the effective fusion of diverse candidate data thus providing interpretability. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are able to represent relationships among candidates, skills and organizations in the data which can enhance fairness as well as prediction performance. In addition, the DeepProbLog block integrates ethical fairness constraints to counteract inherent biases of neural prediction models and Trust-Aware Human Feedback Engine reacts dynamically to recruiter's inputs thus substantially increasing acceptance and trust. The ablation study verifies that each component adds a unique contribution, and the full model gains synergy effect which no

Collectively, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating symbolic reasoning, multimodal learning, relational modeling, and human-in-the-loop feedback in developing a fair recruitment AI system that not only achieves good accuracy but also respects ethical guidelines and humans' social expectations providing a strong foundation for transparent, equitable and trust-sensitive human-AI collaboration in hiring scenarios. VI Conclusion This paper introduces NeuroTrustNet, a neuro-symbolic multimodal system for transparent, fair, and trusted AI-assisted recruitment. This framework combines Cross-Modal Alignment Networks (CMAN) for semantic fusion, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to perform the relational reasoning, DeepProbLog for enforcing ethical rules and Trust-Aware Human Feedback Engine in order to adapt to dynamic changes in recruiter’s feedback. Experimental results on two multimodal recruitment datasets show the superiority and effectiveness of our approach, with 95.3% fairness compliance rate, 93.7 decision interpretability rate, 92.5% recruiter acceptance rate and overall better predictive power 94.6% than five popular conventional neural/hybrid models by a margin of 12-18%. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons, ablation studies, and NTI decompositions all demonstrate that these three components work in synergy to create ethically aligned and interpretable recruiting systems. The attention analysis also shows that the model is able to weigh different types of inputs across modalities such as voice, image and text without ignoring behavioural cues. In summary, NeuroTrustNet shows that joining neural perception with the symbolic reasoning and human-in-the-loop guidance leads to a strong, trust-aware, and ethically sound recruitment pipeline. Future work may also investigate scaling the framework to larger cross-industry datasets, adapting bias debiasing strategies in our model, or generalizing interactive reinforcement learning for continuous recruiter-AI evolving, which can further align human values and AI decision-making.
